extracted.intended_audience: members of the public, consumer stakeholders, and other interested parties who may want to submit comments to the CFPB
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on what notices the CFPB posts for public comment, who may comment, where notices are published, how to submit comments, and how to find archived notices and previously submitted comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of CFPB notices open for public comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The CFPB requests public comment on a wide variety of topics to inform our work. These requests can include: proposed rules, requests for information, and Paperwork Reduction Act notices that give the public an opportunity to comment on potential information collections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This lists the principal categories of agency actions that will be opened for public input; consult the specific notice for full scope and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication venue for notices
rubrics_metrics.description: All these notices will be published in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal Register publication is the official vehicle for CFPB notices; the Federal Register entry will include official dates and procedural details (e.g., comment deadlines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted methods for submitting comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can submit comments online at Regulations.gov, by email, by mail, and by hand delivery/courier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For details (such as mailing addresses, email addresses, or docket numbers) click on the link for the specific notice on which you’d like to comment; follow the submission instructions in that notice to ensure your comment is properly filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may comment / no expertise required
rubrics_metrics.description: You don’t have to be an expert or a lawyer to give comments. We invite all individuals to share their views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau explicitly welcomes input from any member of the public; comments from laypeople, consumers, advocates, industry, and other stakeholders are all appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find currently open notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Browse all notices currently open for comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CFPB’s listing of open notices to identify active dockets and their deadlines; each listed notice links to the specific submission instructions and related documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to closed notices and posted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You can also access notices with comment periods that have already closed and read comments posted to Regulations.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CFPB provides an archive of closed notices and links to comments received (typically via Regulations.gov), enabling review of past submissions and agency records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice-specific details govern submission
rubrics_metrics.description: For details, click on the link for the notice on which you’d like to comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural requirements (format, required docket identifiers, confidentiality claims, PRA information collection details, and precise deadlines) are specified on each notice page; always follow the notice-level instructions rather than only general guidance.
